## Part A: the report as received

1. Study Overview: NCT04547998 (RECELL for Stable Vitiligo)

NCT04547998 (Avita Medical Protocol CTP009, also referred to as the pivotal RSVP trial) is "A Prospective Blinded Within-Subject Randomized Controlled Clinical Study to Investigate the Safety and Effectiveness of RECELL for Repigmentation of Stable Vitiligo Lesions" (NCT04547998; NCT04547998 SAP; PMID: 40042162, DOI: 10.1080/13696998.2025.2475674).

⚬ Population & Design: Adults "18 years of age or older" with "Focal, segmental or generalized (i.e., nonsegmental) stable vitiligo" (no new or expanding lesions "within the preceding 12 months", verified via photographic documentation by an independent Screening Committee) who had not satisfactorily responded to topical therapy and "a minimum of 3 months of phototherapy" (NCT04547998). Each participant contributed "two study areas" ("between 16cm2 and 456cm2 (contiguous)", "of similar size (±50%)", "judged clinically as ≥90% depigmented (by area)") randomly assigned within-subject to either:
  ⚬ Investigational arm: "Spray-On Skin™ Cells prepared using RECELL will be applied to an area prepared by ablative laser, followed by targeted narrowband UVB phototherapy" (NCT04547998).
  ⚬ Control arm: "Control Intervention (UVB)" alone (NCT04547998).
⚬ Enrollment & Registry Timeline: "25" subjects were analyzed ("The safety population consists of all 25 subjects", FDA PMA BP220799 Instructions for Use [IFU]; "Among 25 subjects", Hamzavi et al., 2024, PMID: 39182674, DOI: 10.1016/j.jaad.2024.08.027). Baseline mean affected area was "5.3% of total body surface area (TBSA) (range 0.3-28.8% TBSA)" (FDA PMA BP220799 IFU). Registry milestones on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04547998): First Submitted "2020-09-08", First Posted "2020-09-14", Results First Submitted "2023-07-24", Results First Posted "2023-09-21", Last Update Posted "2024-05-24".
⚬ Follow-up Length After Treatment: "52 weeks" ("duration of his/her participation in the study (52 weeks)", NCT04547998; "A final report summarizing all results through 52 weeks will be completed at this time and submitted to FDA to close out the study", NCT04547998 SAP; "Repigmentation durability was assessed at week-52", Hamzavi et al., 2024, PMID: 39182674).

2. Registered Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Outcomes (NCT04547998)

Primary Outcome Measure (1 Registered)

⚬ Incidence of ≥80% Study Area Repigmentation — Time Frame: "Week 24" (NCT04547998).
  ⚬ Definition: "Repigmentation was evaluated by qualified members of a Central Review Committee." (NCT04547998). The Statistical Analysis Plan specifies: "The study's primary effectiveness endpoint is proportion of responders for RECELL-treated areas versus Control at Week 24. Responders are defined as study areas achieving ≥ 80% pigmentation as determined by the Central Review Committee" tested against "HA: πR – πC > 0.10 (or 10%)" (NCT04547998 SAP).

Secondary Outcome Measures (2 Registered; Fixed Hierarchical Testing)

Per the NCT04547998 SAP, "Each of the secondary effectiveness endpoints will be tested in a fixed hierarchical method at a one-sided 0.025 significance level in the above order":

1. Repigmentation Category — Time Frame: "Week 24" (NCT04547998).
  ⚬ Definition: "Expert Central Review Committee categorization of the amount of area repigmented (0-25%, 26-50%, 51-79% and 80-100%). This is visual estimation of the vitiligo lesion area that has repigmented, with reference to training images. Higher %repigmentation is a better outcome." (NCT04547998).
2. Color Matching — Time Frame: "Week 24" (NCT04547998).
  ⚬ Definition: "The Expert Central Review Committee visually judged the quality of repigmentation in terms of how closely it matches with the normal pigmentation seen in the surrounding area. The rating scale consists of poor, moderate, good, and excellent. Color matching can only be evaluated in instances of >0% repigmentation." (NCT04547998).

Tertiary / Exploratory Measures (Registered in NCT04547998 SAP)

From the retrieved NCT04547998 SAP excerpts, tertiary/exploratory endpoints included:

⚬ "Investigator assessment of pigmentation responder (≥ 80% pigmentation) for the study areas at Week 24" (NCT04547998 SAP).
⚬ "Investigator assessment of repigmentation category (0-25%, 26-50%, 51-79%, and 80-100%) for the study areas at Week 24" (NCT04547998 SAP).
⚬ "CRC and investigator assessment of pigmentation for the study areas at Weeks 36 and 52" and durability at Week 52 ("confirm that... ≥ 80% of the pigmentation remains relative to the subject's Week 24 photograph", NCT04547998 SAP).
⚬ "Investigator assessment of color matching for the study areas" (NCT04547998 SAP).
⚬ "CRC assessment of color matching for the study areas at Weeks 36 and 52" (NCT04547998 SAP).
⚬ "Patient Global Impression of Change-Vitiligo (PaGIC-V)" (NCT04547998 SAP).
⚬ (Items numbered 1, 2, 6, and items beyond 10 in the SAP tertiary list were not found in the retrieved excerpts.)

3. Exact Methodology for "Color Matching" in NCT04547998

⚬ Instrument / Modality: Visual evaluation of "standardized digital photographs" (FDA PMA BP220799 IFU; NCT04547998 SAP) comparing the repigmented lesion to "the normal pigmentation seen in the surrounding area" (NCT04547998). No optical colorimeter, chromameter, or spectrophotometric device was reported (NCT04547998; NCT04547998 SAP).
⚬ Scale & Eligibility Rule: A 4-point ordinal visual scale coded 0–3: "color matching rating category (0-3: poor, moderate, good, excellent)" (NCT04547998 SAP), restricted strictly to repigmented lesions ("Color matching can only be evaluated in instances of >0% repigmentation", NCT04547998). Explicit operational definitions distinguishing "poor", "moderate", "good", and "excellent" (e.g., whether hyper- vs. hypopigmentation was scored symmetrically) were not found in the retrieved NCT04547998 text (though Avita Medical's earlier feasibility protocol NCT04271501 used the same 0–3 scale "inclusive of hypopigmentation and hyperpigmentation").
⚬ Who Rated It: For the registered secondary endpoint at Week 24 and exploratory Week 36/52 endpoints, the "Expert Central Review Committee" (CRC), governed "under a charter that will be approved by the committee, and that will contain the guidance and rules under which they will review and adjudicate data" (NCT04547998; NCT04547998 SAP). Site investigators also performed an exploratory "Investigator assessment of color matching" (NCT04547998 SAP). The exact number of CRC reviewers and their adjudication tie-breaking rule were not found in the retrieved excerpts.
⚬ Blinding: "central evaluator-blinded" (FDA PMA BP220799 SSED and IFU); the CRC was blinded to treatment allocation when rating photographs, whereas treating investigators and subjects were not described as blinded to laser ablation plus RECELL versus UVB-only control (FDA PMA BP220799 SSED; NCT04547998).
⚬ Time Points: Registered secondary endpoint at "Week 24" (NCT04547998); exploratory CRC assessments at "Weeks 36 and 52" (NCT04547998 SAP).

4. Posted and Published Results for Each Outcome (NCT04547998)

Although ClinicalTrials.gov records "Results First Posted: 2023-09-21" (NCT04547998), full tabular results from the ClinicalTrials.gov Results tab were only partially indexed across retrieved primary documents (FDA PMA BP220799 SSED/IFU, Hamzavi et al., 2024 [PMID: 39182674], and Benner et al., 2025 [PMID: 40042162]).

⚬ Primary Outcome (Incidence of ≥80% Study Area Repigmentation at Week 24):
  ⚬ RECELL + Ablative Laser + NB-UVB: "Nine of the 25 (36%) RECELL areas had ≥ 80% repigmentation" (FDA PMA BP220799 SSED & IFU). "None of the RECELL or control areas achieved 100% repigmentation" (FDA PMA BP220799 IFU).
  ⚬ Control (NB-UVB alone): "none of the 25 control areas had ≥ 80% repigmentation" (0%; FDA PMA BP220799 SSED & IFU).
  ⚬ Statistical significance: "Among 25 subjects, 36% of ASCS-treated lesions achieved ≥80% repigmentation at week-24 compared to 0% for Control (P < . 025)" (Hamzavi et al., 2024, PMID: 39182674, DOI: 10.1016/j.jaad.2024.08.027). Benner et al. (PMID: 40042162, DOI: 10.1080/13696998.2025.2475674) reports the exact p-value for the pivotal RSVP trial as "(p = 0.012)".
⚬ Secondary Outcome 1 (Repigmentation Category: 0–25%, 26–50%, 51–79%, 80–100% at Week 24):
  ⚬ Aggregated threshold (>50% repigmentation): "The percentage of repigmentation assessment indicated that 56% of RECELL areas achieved >50% repigmentation versus 12% of control areas" (FDA PMA BP220799 SSED & IFU).
  ⚬ Individual four-bin counts (0–25%, 26–50%, 51–79%, 80–100%) and secondary-endpoint p-value: Apart from the 80–100% bin ("Nine of the 25 (36%)" vs. "none of the 25" [0%], FDA PMA BP220799 IFU), the exact separate counts/percentages for 0–25%, 26–50%, and 51–79% were not found verbatim in the retrieved primary NCT, FDA, or PubMed/DOI excerpts.
⚬ Secondary Outcome 2 (Color Matching at Week 24):
  ⚬ Exact numerical results (poor, moderate, good, excellent counts/percentages and statistical test): Not found verbatim in the retrieved primary excerpts of NCT04547998, FDA PMA BP220799 SSED/IFU, or the PMID: 39182674 abstract.
⚬ Week 52 Durability & Exploratory Outcomes:
  ⚬ Durability: Hamzavi et al. (2024, PMID: 39182674) states "with durability through week-52", and Benner et al. (PMID: 40042162, DOI: 10.1080/13696998.2025.2475674) references "80% of repigmentation still apparent) at Week 52" and notes "at Week 24, treating physicians reported a 68% success rate and 80% of patients self..." (truncated). Exact Week 52 responder counts, Week 36/52 Color Matching distributions, and PaGIC-V distributions were not found verbatim in the retrieved primary excerpts.
⚬ Safety / Adverse Events: "The safety population consists of all 25 subjects" (FDA PMA BP220799 IFU). Hamzavi et al. (2024, PMID: 39182674) reports "The safety profile of ASCS was acceptable". Procedure-associated potential adverse effects listed in the SSED include "scarring, erythema, Koebner phenomenon, pruritus, and worsening vitiligo" (FDA PMA BP220799 SSED); exact per-event TEAE counts for the 25-subject cohort were not found in the retrieved excerpts.

6. Other Registered Trials in Vitiligo, Piebaldism, or Other Pigment Loss Using a Colour-Match Outcome

No registered trials specifically targeting piebaldism, idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis (IGH), or nevus depigmentosus alone with a color-match outcome were found on ClinicalTrials.gov. Eight additional registered trials—six in vitiligo, one in vitiligo / depigmented scars / depigmentation, and one in stable non-vitiligo leukoderma—were identified with an explicit color-match outcome:

1. NCT04271501 (RECELL vs. MKTP Feasibility Study; Avita Medical — Stable Vitiligo):
  ⚬ Condition & Design: "50 matched, stable depigmented areas from 10 subjects" with stable vitiligo (≥ 22 years), comparing MKTP + UVB vs. RECELL (1:5, 1:10, 1:20 dilutions) + UVB (NCT04271501).
  ⚬ Color-match outcome & method: "Blinded Evaluator Color Matching" — "Assessment of color matching (0-3: poor, moderate, good, excellent) inclusive of hypopigmentation and hyperpigmentation", rated by "a Blinded Evaluator (blinded to treatment allocation) using standardized photographs" (NCT04271501).
  ⚬ Time points & Results: "4, 12 and 24 weeks". Results: Not found ("Suspended and Terminated to focus on CTP009 (NCT04547998)", NCT04271501).
2. NCT06804811 (Ruxolitinib Cream 0.75% / 1.5% vs. Vehicle; Incyte Corporation — Pediatric Nonsegmental Vitiligo):
  ⚬ Condition: Nonsegmental vitiligo in children "Aged 6 to < 12 years" (NCT06804811).
  ⚬ Color-match outcome & method: Secondary outcome "Proportion of participants in each category for the color-matching question" — "a patient-reported measure of vitiligo treatment success that has a 5-point scale" (NCT06804811). Exact category anchors and blinding details were not found in the retrieved excerpt.

**Labels.** FOUND = the quote or fact is in the named source word for word. FOUND, DIFFERS = the source supports it but the wording, attribution or detail differs (difference stated). NOT CHECKABLE = the named source could not be read here (reason stated). DOES NOT MATCH = the source says something else.

### B.2 NCT04547998: posted results the report did not find

The registry's Results section posts all three outcomes. Quoted exactly from the API record (`resultsSection.outcomeMeasuresModule`). Analysis population "ITT"; groups "Control Intervention (UVB)" and "Investigational Intervention (Ablative Laser Resurfacing + RECELL + UVB)".

**Primary, "Incidence of ≥80% Study Area Repigmentation", Week 24, unit "study areas":** Control 0 of 25, RECELL 9 of 25. Analysis: "SUPERIORITY", p "0.012", method "continuity-corrected method".

**Secondary, "Repigmentation Category", Week 24, unit "depigmented vitiligo lesions" (25 per arm):**

| Category (registry wording) | Control | RECELL |
|---|---|---|
| Repigmentation Category: 0% | 5 | 3 |
| Repigmentation Category: 1 to 25% | 13 | 6 |
| Repigmentation Category: 26 to 50% | 4 | 2 |
| Repigmentation Category: 51 to 79% | 3 | 5 |
| Repigmentation Category: 80 to 99% | 0 | 9 |
| Repigmentation Category: 100% | 0 | 0 |

p "<0.001", "Wilcoxon (Mann-Whitney)"; comment: "P-value based on Wilcoxon signed rank test at 2-sided 0.05 significance level." [The >50% shares the report quotes from the FDA documents follow from these counts: RECELL 5 + 9 = 14 of 25 = 56%; control 3 + 0 = 3 of 25 = 12%.]

**Secondary, "Color Matching", Week 24, unit "study areas with >0% repigmentation" (Control 20, RECELL 22):**

| Color Matching Category | Control | RECELL |
|---|---|---|
| Poor | 0 | 1 |
| Moderate | 4 | 6 |
| Good | 12 | 9 |
| Excellent | 4 | 6 |

p "1.000", "Wilcoxon (Mann-Whitney)"; comment: "2-sided (0.05 significance level), based on 19 participants with assessable color matching outcomes for both treatments".

[Plain reading, not in the source: among areas that regained any pigment, the blinded committee rated the colour match of RECELL areas no better than that of UVB-only areas at Week 24. The graded colour match is of whatever pigment returned, not of the whole area: a control area with a few percent repigmentation can score "Excellent".]

The registry posts **no** Week 36 or Week 52 results, and no colour-match result after Week 24.

### B.3 NCT05750823: posted colour-match result the report missed

Results were posted 2026-03-20. The colour-match question, quoted: "At this point of your treatment, how well does your genital skin color match between your treated vitiligo skin and normal skin?: Responses: (1) excellent, (2) very good, (3) good, (4) poor, or (5) very poor." Participants were "shown their baseline genital photograph for reference". Single arm, "Ruxolitinib 1.5% Cream BID", applied "for up to 48 weeks"; masking "NONE". Population "Full Analysis Set. Only participants with available data were analyzed."

| Week (analysed n) | Excellent | Very good | Good | Poor | Very poor |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Part C: judgment (this thread's reading, not a source)

Everything in this part is interpretation. None of these trials is about IGH, so none of it enters the Module 1 ledger. The measurement plan (`content/measurement-tool-plan.md`) and the study proposal (`content/study-proposal.md`, PR 6) are **not edited**; the suggestions below are for Ben to accept or drop.

### C.1 How these trials defined and rated colour match

1. **Every colour-match outcome is a human judgment on a coarse scale.** Expert panels on photographs (NCT04547998, NCT04271501, NCT07953686), unspecified visual grading (NCT03717025, NCT03668834, NCT02038257, NCT07662915), or the patient's own answer (NCT06804811, NCT05750823). None names a colorimeter, spectrophotometer or any calculated colour difference.
2. **Scales lose direction or detail.** The RECELL scale (poor to excellent) does not say whether a mismatch is too light or too dark; only the earlier Avita protocol says its 0–3 scale is "inclusive of hypopigmentation and hyperpigmentation". The PGIMER trials keep direction ("somewhat lighter than", "same as", "somewhat darker than") but have only three steps.
3. **Colour match is graded only where pigment came back.** NCT04547998: "Color matching can only be evaluated in instances of >0% repigmentation", so the two arms are compared on different sets of areas (20 vs 22; 19 pairs). The match describes the returned pigment, not whether the area as a whole now looks like skin.
4. **No time point is counted from the final treatment.** RECELL's "Week 24" is counted from the procedure, and NB-UVB then "will commence on both study areas after dressings are no longer in place", with no stated end in the documents read. Ruxolitinib's Week 48 is the end of treatment. Under rule 2 the time since the final treatment is NOT_DERIVABLE for every trial here. The registry posts no colour-match result beyond Week 24 for RECELL.
5. **The one posted head-to-head colour-match result is null.** RECELL raised the number of areas with ≥80% repigmentation from 0 of 25 to 9 of 25, yet the blinded colour-match grades did not differ (p "1.000"). [Two readings fit: the pigment that returns matches about equally well whatever brought it back, or a four-step grade on 19 pairs cannot detect a difference. The data cannot separate them.] Either way it supports the project's rule that area coverage and colour match are separate outcomes.

### C.2 What an instrument-based measure would add

- **A number for every spot, including failures.** ΔL\* and ΔE00 against the ring are defined whether or not any pigment returned, so there is no conditioning on response and no shrinking denominator.
- **Sensitivity.** A continuous difference with a known smallest detectable change can show a small but real difference that four categories on 19 pairs cannot, and can show "no difference" with a stated margin instead of a bare p = 1.
- **Direction.** Signed ΔL\* shows overshoot to dark, which the RECELL scale does not separate from under-correction.
- **Stability over time.** The same calibrated measurement at 6 months is comparable to the baseline one; a panel grading photographs years apart can drift.
- **A fit to small spots.** Area bins (0–25%, 26–50%…) suit large vitiligo patches (16 to 456 cm² in RECELL). An IGH spot of a few millimetres is more naturally described by its contrast than by percent area.
- **What it does not replace:** whether people can see the difference. The panel and patient questions below remain the way to set the match threshold.

### C.3 Suggestions (not applied)

For the measurement plan:

1. **Section 7 (prior art):** record that none of the nine registered colour-match trials checked here uses an instrument; all are graded by eye or by the patient.
2. **Section 2.3 (`T_match`):** name the VGICG "reference atlas … depicting vitiligo repigmentation patterns and color match" (cited in the NCT04547998 SAP) as a candidate anchor for perceptibility, to be searched and quoted before use.
3. **Rung 3 validation:** add agreement between the instrument's ΔE00 / ΔL\* and a blinded three-rater panel using a RECELL-style poor/moderate/good/excellent grade, adjudicated 2 of 3 as in that SAP, so the instrument can be related to the grade clinicians already use.

For the study proposal:

4. **Section 3.1:** say explicitly that the colour endpoint is computed for every spot, including spots with no repigmentation, unlike NCT04547998.
5. **Section 3.4:** keep the blinded panel grade as a secondary outcome and report it alongside the computed endpoint, using a scale that keeps direction (for example lighter / same / darker plus a quality grade).
6. **Secondary outcome:** add a patient-reported colour-match question. The Incyte wording (excellent / very good / good / poor / very poor) is registered and could be adapted.
7. **Definition of "final treatment":** state that any adjunct (phototherapy, creams) counts as treatment, so the six-month clock starts only when everything stops. RECELL shows how a single-procedure trial can still carry on treating for an unstated time.
8. **Section 2 (the gap):** note, as context outside the ledger, that the only registered colour-match result found (RECELL, vitiligo) is at Week 24 from the procedure and is null between arms.
9. **Watch:** NCT07662915 (non-vitiligo leukoderma, MKTP or Jodhpur technique plus excimer, "Color Match Assessment" at 6 months, outcome assessor masked) is the registered trial closest to IGH, but its record does not name IGH and recruitment has not started.
